title: Invented Magazines

description.main: Duncan Hannah's final series of paintings, imagined covers for mid-century film and pop magazines, published by Dashwood Books in 2022 shortly after the artist's death. The 48-page staple-bound volume reproduces the paintings in colour with Hannah's own account of the project and a text by Arthur Fournier.
description.extended:
A staple-bound volume of Duncan Hannah's final series of paintings: imagined covers for the film and pop magazines of his youth, published by Dashwood Books in October 2022, four months after his death.

Hannah began the series in March 2020, locked down in Cornwall, Connecticut. He worked from a trunk of European film magazines collected since the 1970s, titles like Continental Film Review, Ciné Revue and Playmen. He borrowed the logos of real, mostly defunct magazines and painted his favourite actors and musicians beneath them. He called the results "highly subjective dream magazine covers," a form of Pop Art in the line of his earlier Penguin paperback paintings. The book reproduces the paintings in colour across 48 pages, with Hannah's own account of the project and a short text by Arthur Fournier. Hannah finalised the edit shortly before he died in June 2022.

Hannah (1952–2022) grew up in Minneapolis and studied at Bard and Parsons. He was a fixture of downtown New York in the 1970s and appeared in Amos Poe's Unmade Beds. His notebooks from that decade were published as Twentieth-Century Boy (Knopf, 2018). Kasmin's posthumous exhibition Duncan Hannah: On Paper (2023) included works from this series.
description.artist_bio: Duncan Hannah (Minneapolis 1952 - West Cornwall, Connecticut, 2022) studied at Bard College and Parsons School of Design (graduated 1975). A figure in the downtown New York scene of the 1970s, he ran the Television fan club, appeared in Amos Poe's Unmade Beds (1976) and The Foreigner (1978), and showed in the 1980 Times Square Show. His painting has been described as romantic realist. His Penguin paperback series began in 2008; the Invented Magazines series, begun in 2020, was his last. His 1970s notebooks were published as Twentieth-Century Boy (Knopf, 2018) and serialized in the Paris Review. Work in the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Shown at Half Gallery (Early Days, 2017) and, posthumously, Kasmin (On Paper, 2023).

notes: No ISBN on any source (Dashwood listing, dstrettell.com, Printed Matter); cover filename uses _2440 placeholder. Dimensions conflict: the Dashwood listing says 6.625 x 9.5 in, but Dashwood's own publications site (dstrettell.com) says 6 x 8.25 in and Printed Matter says 15.5 x 21 cm; the cropped cover's aspect ratio (0.71) also fits 6 x 8.25, so height_cm 21 / width_cm 15.5 recorded. Release date October 2022 per dstrettell.com. Publisher note on dstrettell.com: Hannah died suddenly in early summer 2022 just after finalizing the edit. duncanhannah.com is live (200) and has an Invented Magazines gallery of 60 works at 14 x 11 in. Half Gallery page is a 2017 exhibition (Early Days), not a representation page. Cover is a 500 px product shot on patterned cloth, deskewed about 1.2 degrees and cropped; no larger image exists (Printed Matter reuses the same photos). Not signed. No LOC/WorldCat record searched: small-press edition of 500 without ISBN.
